story:
<!-- Case: F2L-01-FR -->

## Overview
Classic solved pair hovering above the Front Right slot—align it and drop it in while keeping every other slot untouched.

## Recognition
- Corner sticker with the D color points upward and sits directly above its matching edge.
- Viewed from the front, the pair forms a clean 2×1 block with matching side colors.
- Rotating the block over FR keeps both stickers facing the correct directions; any mismatch signals a different case.

## Technique
1. Use light `U`/`U'` adjustments to center the block over FR.
2. Apply the standard insert `R U' R'` to slide it into the slot intact.
3. If FR was filled, eject with `R U R'`, realign, then insert.

## Fingertricks
- Keep the right wrist neutral and treat `R U' R'` as a single packet so you can look ahead.
- Use a gentle right-index push for `U'` to avoid cube rotations.

## Common Mistakes
- Rushing the insert before the block is perfectly aligned, causing misoriented stickers.
- Forgetting to clear the FR slot before inserting, which forces an extra eject.

## Practice
- Run 10 slow reps focusing on zero pauses between alignment and insert; then aim for sub‑0.8s.
- Track recognition time—flag in SRS if it takes more than ~2 seconds to spot.

## Related Cases
- [F2L-01-FL](deddal://case/F2L-01-FL) – Mirror solved with `L' U L`.
- [F2L-02-FR](deddal://case/F2L-02-FR) – Same block but positioned over the wrong slot.

## Pro Tips
- Because the cube stays in home orientation, this is a perfect moment to scan for your next pair during the insert.

title: F2L 2

story:
<!-- Case: F2L-02-FR -->

## Overview
Solved pair is parked over the wrong slot; rotate or mentally reorient, place it using left-style moves, then return to home orientation.

## Recognition
- Paired block hovers above FL instead of FR even though both stickers match.
- From the FR viewpoint, the pair’s stickers face left, signaling that a y-rotation will fix alignment.
- After performing `y'`, no D-color sticker points up—the block is ready to drop straight down.

## Technique
1. Execute a quick `y'` (or rotate your perspective) so the block now sits over FR.
2. Insert with `U' (R' U R)`—the mirrored sequence keeps the pair intact.
3. Undo the rotation (`y`) to resume your standard orientation.

## Fingertricks
- Some solvers swap the `y'` for an `Lw'` push to avoid full cube rotations.
- Focus on keeping the block centered during `U'` so the mirrored insert feels natural.

## Common Mistakes
- Forgetting to undo the rotation, which throws off recognition for the next pair.
- Forcing the insert without aligning first, causing the block to land twisted.

## Practice
- Drill 10 reps alternating between this case and F2L-01-FR to stay comfortable with both orientations.
- Try solving it using an `Lw'` substitute to see which ergonomics feel faster.

## Related Cases
- [F2L-01-FR](deddal://case/F2L-01-FR) – Already aligned; no rotation needed.
- [F2L-02-FL](deddal://case/F2L-02-FL) – Mirror target on the left.

## Pro Tips

<!-- Case: F2L-03-FR -->

## Overview
Keyhole insert where the corner sits in FR facing you and the matching edge rests above it; open the slot, pair them, and close it again without disturbing other slots.

## Recognition
- Front face shows a vertical 1×2 bar (edge on top, corner already in FR).
- The corner’s white sticker looks straight at you, indicating it’s flipped in place.
- The top edge’s sticker matches the front center, so opening the slot will not break other pairs.

## Technique
1. Execute `F'` to pull the corner out and create a temporary keyhole.
2. Use `U'` (or `U`) to align the edge with its center while the slot is open.
3. Close with `F` to lock the paired block back into FR.

## Fingertricks
- Push `F'`/`F` with the right index to keep the cube stable.
- Use the left index for `U'` so the right hand can stay anchored on the R face.

## Common Mistakes
- Closing the slot before the edge is aligned, which recreates the same flipped setup.
- Over-rotating the front face and disturbing adjacent solved pieces.

## Practice
- Drill slow reps emphasizing calm `F'`/`F` turns to avoid cube wobble.
- Alternate with F2L-10 to get comfortable managing flipped-in-slot corners.

## Related Cases

## Overview
Corner and edge are separated in the top layer with different colors facing up—a classic disconnected pair requiring a setup move to bring them together.

## Recognition
- Corner and edge both sit in the U layer with non-matching top colors.
- Edge orientation is correct (white/yellow not on top).
- Pair needs one move to connect before inserting.

## Technique
1. Position the corner above the target slot.
2. Execute `U R U' R'` to pair and insert in one sequence.
3. The U move brings edge into position, R connects them, U' separates temporarily, R' inserts the pair.

## Fingertricks
- Use right index finger for U push.
- Flow smoothly: U (index push) → R (thumb push) → U' (index flick) → R' (thumb pull).
- Keep movements tight without pauses.

## Common Mistakes
- Not aligning the corner correctly before starting—verify position first.
- Breaking rhythm between moves—practice as one flowing sequence.
- Rotating cube unnecessarily—this case solves from one angle.

## Practice
- Drill 20 reps focusing on smooth U → R → U' → R' flow.
- Time yourself: aim for under 1 second execution.
- Practice recognition by scrambling specifically to this pattern.

## Related Cases

story:

## Overview
Hide-and-reinsert scenario: both pieces sit in FR but mispaired, so you eject, realign with `U` moves, and reinsert.

## Recognition
- Both corner and edge occupy FR yet the edge orientation is wrong.
- Corner location is correct but its relationship to the edge is twisted.
- Requires breaking the slot apart before any clean insertion can happen.

## Technique
1. **Break** – Use `U R U' R'` (or your preferred eject) to remove the corner and edge.
2. **Reposition** – Adjust with `U`/`U'` so the edge sits above its matching center and the corner is ready to pair.
3. **Insert** – Perform the standard `R U' R'` insert to place the newly paired block.

## Fingertricks
- Keep the right wrist relaxed so the eject and insert packets flow without pauses.
- Use light `U` flicks to realign the pieces instead of full rotations.

## Common Mistakes
- Failing to fully separate the pair, leading to a repeated mispair.
- Forgetting to restore the U-layer alignment before reinsert.

## Practice
- Alternate between eject-and-insert drills until the sequence feels automatic.
- Record solves to ensure the eject + alignment + insert stays under 1.5s.

## Related Cases
- [F2L-10-FL](deddal://case/F2L-10-FL) – Mirror version on the left slot.

## Pro Tips
- Focus on the alignment step: spotting where the edge needs to be before reinserting speeds up every hide-and-repair case.

## Overview
Disconnected FR case with the cross color on top and a badly oriented edge; you must position both pieces relative to each other before pairing.

## Recognition
- Corner and edge are separated—nothing is paired yet.
- Corner’s white sticker points up while the edge’s cross color also faces up (bad orientation).

## Technique
1. **Set up** – Use `U`/`U'` to place the corner above its target slot and the edge above its matching center, forming an “L” separation.
2. **Pair** – Perform `R U R'` (or `U R U' R'`) to bring the corner out next to the edge.
3. **Insert** – Convert to a standard paired insert (`U' R U' R'` or whatever your preferred sequence is) once the block is formed.

## Fingertricks
- Keep the right wrist loose so you can chain `R U R'` packets while watching the edge.
- Use pre-turned `U` moves to minimize pauses before the final insert.

## Common Mistakes
- Trying to insert before the edge orientation is fixed, leading to another disconnected case.
- Forgetting to track both pieces, which causes unnecessary cube rotations.

## Practice
- Drill “separate → pair → insert” slowly, ensuring you always know the edge location before starting.
- Aim to reduce look-up time: verbalize “corner here, edge there” before moving.

## Related Cases
- [F2L-20-FL](deddal://case/F2L-20-FL) – Mirror variant for the left slot.

## Pro Tips
- Think in terms of relative positions (edge left/right of corner). Once you know the relationship, you can use muscle-memory pairing instead of memorizing dozens of algs.
